§6Iodine-131§f

§aExtremely radioactive fission product, roughly 6.3% of short-lived nuclear waste.§f

§bIodine-131§f (Radioiodine) is an extremely radioactive and hazardous iodine isotope. It is naturally pyrophoric, meaning it can spontaneously ignite in air.

§6Production§f:
§b• Short-Lived Nuclear Waste§f, I-131 makes up approximately 6.3% of short-lived waste on average

§6Where It Comes From§f:
I-131 is produced during nuclear fission of uranium and plutonium fuels. When you reprocess spent fuel in the §bPUREX§f, or let fuel rods decay in a §bSpent Fuel Pool Drum§f, the short-lived waste you get contains this isotope among others.

§cWARNING:§f I-131 is extremely radioactive. Wear radiation-resistant armor when handling short-lived nuclear waste, and store it in proper containment.

§ePS:§f While I-131 has limited direct use, it contributes significantly to the overall radioactivity of short-lived waste. Processing it through waste disposal drums or the SILEX is the way to manage it.
